raw_graphql_pull_request.body: # Multi-trace analysis on `combine_by_node` This PR adds the `combine_by_node` aggregation and moves the agent's multi_trace report onto it. Until now, multi_trace stopped after the per-job reports. `combine_by_node` stacks one block of CSV rows per node instead of summing them. The multi_trace report was written for summed data and would get several numbers wrong on stacked data: - The manifest's GPU utilization takes whichever row comes last. - Top Operations adds time across nodes, and its op counts grow with the number of nodes. - The fallback divides by surviving kernel time. - The priority-consistency check sums per-node findings. `node` is now the one identity from the YAML through to `analysis.json`. The report uses two denominators: - **T**, one node's captured GPU time. Every number a reader sees uses T. - **T_all**, the sum over nodes. Ranking, `impact_score`, `pct_e2e` and every gate use T_all. On a single trace T equals T_all, so the single-trace report does not change. ## Change - **Aggregation.** In `Reporting/aggregate_perf_reports.py`, `combine_by_node` is the supported policy. - The aggregated CSVs hold one block per node, tagged with `node` and `phase`. - `Percentage (%)` is a share of that node's kernel time. - `gpu_timeline` ends with an `all` block summed over the nodes. A node named `all` is rejected. - **Config.** Changed in `Reporting/generate_perf_report_from_config.py` and `utils/config_utils.py`. - Under `combine_by_node`, the YAML `node` is required and is a non-negative index within its phase. - The node id is `_` (`prefill_0`), and a job's `name` defaults to it. - `phase` must match `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`. - The resolved config re-runs unchanged. - multi_trace requires `combine_by_node`, rejects two jobs on the same node, and names the focus job by its node id. - **Denominators.** The GPU-utilization reader moves to `category_analyses/analysis_utils.py` as `gpu_utilization_from_timeline(gpu_timeline) -> dict`. - It selects the `all` block by name and adds `nodes{}` with each node's metrics. - The manifest, the per-category metadata and the fallback all read T and T_all from it. - Moving it out of `orchestrator_prepare` also avoids an import cycle with the fallback. - **Report.** Changed in `analysis_template.md`, `sub_agent_spec.md`, `kernel-fusion-analyzer.md`, `reference.md`, `report_utils.py`, `kernel_fusion.py` and `kernel_fusion_analysis.py`. - The Executive Summary has a Total column and one column per node, in job order. - Top Operations is one table per node, with its own `top_ops node=` marker and global ranks. - Each finding carries `**Node**` and `node=` on its markers. - Detail tables show `% of Node` in place of `%E2E`. - Priorities are ranked globally on T_all, with no recommendation cap. - **Plot.** In `utils/plot_utils.py`, `generate_perf_plot` draws one bar per node. Each axis is scaled to that node's time, and each category keeps one color across nodes. Single-trace plots are unchanged. - **Fallback.** Changed in `utils/deterministic_fallback.py`. - With nodes, it reads each node's time from the sibling `gpu_timeline.csv` and writes the per-node Executive Summary, `**Node**` and `% of Node`. - It also fixes a pre-existing double count that affects every scope. Several CSV rows can resolve to the same op, and each became its own P-item carrying the whole group's impact, so `analysis.json` counted that impact more than once. The fallback now writes one P-item per op, and the gate, cap and drop note count ops. - **Validation.** Changed in `utils/validation_utils.py` and `workflow_scripted_evals.py`. - The Executive Summary header must be Total plus the node names, and each node's Total Time must match the manifest. - R4 runs per `top_ops` block. - R6 compares `node` on the card and the detail estimate. - INV7 is keyed on (node, category). - The marker eval checks every `top_ops` block. - **`analysis.json`.** Changed in `post_processing/analysis_json.py` and `candidate_schema.py`. - Tasks carry `node`, which replaces `phase` and is `null` outside multi_trace. - `executive_summary.node_metrics` holds the node columns. - `top_operations` reads every block and stamps `node`. - It also fixes a pre-existing Top Ops parser bug. The parser took cells by position, so it dropped rows without a trailing row comment (unmodeled categories) and shifted the comparative table's columns. Cells now map by header name. - **Docs.** `docs/how-to/agent.md`, `generate-perf-report-from-config.md` and `api-reference.md` describe `combine_by_node` and the node index. - **Example.** `build_docker_vllm.sh` adds vLLM v0.32.0. 31 files changed, 1695 insertions(+), 653 deletions(-). ## Observable effect Single trace: - The report markdown and plot are unchanged. - `analysis.json` tasks carry `"node": null`. - Top Ops rows parse by header. - Fallback reports list each op once. multi_trace, on a two-node inference trace with one prefill node and one decode node: | Metric | Total | decode_0 | prefill_0 | |--------|-------|----------|-----------| | Total Time | 2340.22 ms | 343.79 ms | 1996.42 ms | | Compute % | 99.23% | 99.29% | 99.22% | | Idle % | 0.71% | 0.54% | 0.74% | | Exposed Communication % | 0.00% | 0.00% | 0.00% | | Top Bottleneck Category | GEMM (80.86%) | GEMM (65.35%) | GEMM (83.54%) | Top Operations, one table per node with global ranks: **decode_0** (343.79 ms) | Rank | Category | Time (ms) | % of Compute Time | Ops | |---|---|---|---|---| | 3 | GEMM | 223.076 | 65.35% | 27 | | 4 | InferenceAttention | 81.36 | 23.83% | 4 | **prefill_0** (1996.42 ms) | Rank | Category | Time (ms) | % of Compute Time | Ops | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | GEMM | 1654.717 | 83.54% | 6 | | 2 | InferenceAttention | 166.226 | 8.39% | 1 | | 5 | triton | 147.051 | 7.42% | 7 | Each of the five cards names its node. For example, P1 has `**Node**: prefill_0` and `impact_score: 12.13`, and P3 has `**Node**: decode_0` and `4.8`. P1's detail rows show `% of Node` against prefill_0's 1996.42 ms. The plot has two bars, `decode_0 (343.79 ms)` and `prefill_0 (1996.42 ms)`. In `analysis.json`: - `node_metrics` holds both nodes. - `top_operations` has 5 rows, each with `node`. - P1's `members[].pct_e2e` is unchanged (`time_ms` / Total Time). ## Validation - **New and renamed tests.** These cover: - the per-node aggregation blocks and the `all` total - node ids, defaults and rejections in the config - stacked `gpu_timeline` parsing - per-node findings, priority data and the plot - the validator rules R4, R6 and INV7 and the Executive Summary check - `analysis.json` node fields and header-mapped Top Ops - the fallback's per-node cards and one P-item per op `black` is clean. - **Deterministic run on the two-node trace, without the LLM.** - Findings match the base after the rename. - Node totals are 343.79 and 1996.42 ms, and T_all is 2340.22 ms. - The per-node priorities sum to the base values. - **Agent run on the same trace.** - `validate_report` is clean. - The report and `analysis.json` match the design above. - Every entry module imports in a fresh interpreter. - **Agent end-to-end runs on a set of single-trace cases, compared with `staging_agent`.** - The pass/fail pattern is the same in every case. - Headers are identical, and headline metrics are byte-equal. - Fallback reports differ only by the one-P-item-per-op fix. - The only failing checks also fail on `staging_agent`. - Every report renders to `analysis.json`. - **Downstream reader.** Hyperloom's `analysis.json` and perf-report reader tests pass against this tree with no Hyperloom change.

@devalshahamd  this branch brings in your branch and modifies the node nomenclature

Config (Reporting/generate_perf_report_from_config.py)
  - node is an index. It must be a non-negative integer, the node's index within its phase. Before, it was any non-empty string such as prefill_w0. Booleans and
    negative numbers are rejected.
  - Node id. The id is built as <phase>_<node> (prefill_0) and stored on PlannedJob.node_id. The aggregation now receives node_id instead of the raw node, so the aggregated CSVs label rows prefill_0.
  - name default. Under combine_by_node, name is optional even with several jobs and defaults to the node id. Other policies still require it.
  - phase rule. phase now follows the same character rule as name ([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+), because it becomes part of the node id and the output file names.
We  might have more than 2 nodes in future, or we might do combine_by_phase. Should we have any explicit support for that here?

@devalshahamd  this branch brings in your branch and modifies the node nomenclature

Config (Reporting/generate_perf_report_from_config.py)
  - node is an index. It must be a non-negative integer, the node's index within its phase. Before, it was any non-empty string such as prefill_w0. Booleans and
    negative numbers are rejected.
  - Node id. The id is built as <phase>_<node> (prefill_0) and stored on PlannedJob.node_id. The aggregation now receives node_id instead of the raw node, so the aggregated CSVs label rows prefill_0.
  - name default. Under combine_by_node, name is optional even with several jobs and defaults to the node id. Other policies still require it.
  - phase rule. phase now follows the same character rule as name ([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+), because it becomes part of the node id and the output file names.
